Analytical Measurements
SPM Analyzer: Suspended Particulate Matter Meaning, Measuring Methods, CPCB Limits and SPM Calculation in µg/m³

We measure dust in air as weight per cubic metre, and the instrument you pick decides how far you can trust that number. Below are the sampler, the continuous monitors, the Indian limits and a full calculation you can repeat.

SPM Full Form PM10 and PM2.5 CPCB NAAQS 2009 µg/m³ Calculator Troubleshooting

An SPM analyzer tells you how many micrograms of dust float in each cubic metre of air near a plant, road or city station. You will also find the measuring methods, the CPCB limits, a worked calculation and the faults that spoil a reading.

Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how an SPM analyzer measures suspended particulate matter, which limits apply in India and how to calculate the result in µg/m³.
Quick Answer

What is an SPM analyzer and how does it measure dust in air?

SPM analyzer is the instrument that measures suspended particulate matter, the fine dust and smoke floating in air, as mass concentration in µg/m³. The reference method pulls a known air volume through a filter and weighs the dust: SPM = (W2 minus W1) × 10⁶ ÷ V. For example, 0.27 g of dust collected from 1728 m³ of air gives 156.25 µg/m³.

What Is an SPM Analyzer?

An SPM analyzer is an air monitoring instrument that measures the mass of suspended particulate matter in a known volume of air and reports it in µg/m³. It can be a manual high volume sampler with a lab balance or a continuous monitor that uses beta rays or light to give hourly readings.

Key Facts
  • SPM means suspended particulate matter, reported in µg/m³.
  • India replaced SPM with PM10 and PM2.5 limits in the NAAQS of 18 November 2009.
  • Approved methods are gravimetric, TEOM and beta attenuation.

In Indian plants you find the SPM analyzer at the boundary wall, near coal yards, crushers and kilns, and at city stations. It complements the stack monitors in a continuous emissions monitoring system, which watch the chimney while the ambient unit watches what people breathe.

Do You Know?

The CPCB guideline of April 2003 treats a day with 16 hours or more of valid sampling as representative, and targets at least 104 monitoring days per year at each station.

SPM Full Form and Meaning: TSP, PM10 and PM2.5

SPM full form is suspended particulate matter, which covers every particle that stays airborne long enough to be sampled, roughly up to 25 to 50 µm. PM10 and PM2.5 are size fractions of that same dust, up to 10 µm and 2.5 µm aerodynamic diameter.

TermSizeReachesUsual sampler
SPM or TSPUp to 25 to 50 µmNose and throatHigh volume sampler
RSPM or PM1010 µm and belowUpper lungsRespirable dust sampler with cyclone
PM2.52.5 µm and belowDeep lungLow volume sampler, 16.67 L/min

In the United States the same coarse fraction is called total suspended particulates, and 40 CFR Part 50 Appendix B says the catch depends on wind speed and direction. RSPM, respirable suspended particulate matter, is the older Indian name for PM10.

Quick Tip

When a consent order says SPM, check whether the authority wants TSP, PM10 or PM2.5 data, because the inlet head and the limit both change.

How Does an SPM Analyzer Measure Particulate Matter?

An SPM analyzer measures particulate matter by weighing dust caught on a filter, by the drop in beta rays through a dust spot, or by light scattered from particles. Weighing is the reference, and you check the faster methods against it.

High volume gravimetric

A blower pulls 1.1 to 1.7 m³/min through a glass fibre filter for 24 hours.

Best for: Reference and compliance data
Reference
Beta attenuation

A carbon 14 source measures dust mass on filter tape every hour.

Best for: Continuous stations
Continuous
Light scattering

A laser beam and photodetector estimate mass from scattered light.

Best for: Dust mapping, surveys
Indicative
TEOM

A vibrating tapered element slows down as dust mass builds on it.

Best for: Short average data
Continuous

The high volume sampler is the classic SPM analyzer taught in Indian colleges. Air turns under the gabled roof, passes through a 20.3 by 25.4 cm glass fibre filter and leaves through the motor blower, while a flow meter and timer record the volume.

The US EPA method asks for a filter that catches at least 99 percent of 0.3 µm particles and a flow between 1.1 and 1.7 standard m³/min. A valid run lasts 1440 minutes plus or minus 60 minutes.

A continuous SPM analyzer of the beta type works in hourly cycles. Met One describes the BAM 1020 this way: it counts beta rays through clean tape, pulls air through that spot for the hour, then counts again.

I = I₀ × e^(minus μ × m)
m = (1 ÷ μ) × ln(I₀ ÷ I)
C = m ÷ V

Here I₀ is the count through clean tape, I is the count through the dust spot and m is mass per unit area. The BAM 1020 datasheet lists a 60 µCi source, 16.67 L/min flow, a 0 to 10 mg/m³ range and an hourly detection limit under 4.8 µg/m³.

Light scattering units are cheap, but humidity and particle colour change the scattered light, so they read high on damp days. Treat them like the photoelectric sensors they are and correct them with a site factor from gravimetric samples.

Continuous SPM analyzer: strengths
  • Hourly data shows traffic and loading peaks.
  • Alarms reach the control room by 4 to 20 mA or Modbus.
  • No daily filter handling.
Continuous SPM analyzer: limits
  • Higher cost than a manual sampler.
  • Needs a heated inlet so moisture is not counted as dust.
  • Still needs gravimetric comparison.

CPCB NAAQS Limits for Particulate Matter in India

India sets PM10 at 100 µg/m³ for 24 hours and 60 µg/m³ annual, and PM2.5 at 60 and 40 µg/m³, for all areas under the NAAQS of 18 November 2009. The older SPM limits still appear in textbooks and some old consent conditions.

ParameterAverageIndustrialResidentialSensitive
PM10 (2009)24 hour100100100
PM10 (2009)Annual606060
PM2.5 (2009)24 hour606060
PM2.5 (2009)Annual404040
SPM (old)24 hour500200100
SPM (old)Annual36014070

All values are in µg/m³, and the old SPM figures come from Table A1.1 of the CPCB 2003 guideline. Both versions say 24 hour values must be met 98 percent of the time, and exceedances may not fall on two consecutive monitoring days.

Myth: A clear sky means dust is within limits.
Fact: PM2.5 is invisible, so a clear day can still exceed 60 µg/m³.
Myth: Any SPM analyzer reading can be compared with the PM10 limit.
Fact: Total SPM includes coarse dust above 10 µm, so it always reads higher than PM10.
Myth: A cheap laser sensor matches the lab method.
Fact: Optical sensors need a correction factor from side by side gravimetric runs.

How to Calculate SPM Concentration in µg/m³

To calculate SPM concentration, subtract the clean filter weight from the loaded weight, multiply by 10⁶ to get micrograms and divide by the air volume in m³. The air volume is the average flow multiplied by run time in minutes.

V = Q average × t
SPM = (W2 minus W1) × 10⁶ ÷ V
W1 = 4.2510 g, W2 = 4.5210 g
Q = (1.25 + 1.15) ÷ 2 = 1.20 m³/min
V = 1.20 × 1440 = 1728 m³
SPM = 270000 ÷ 1728 = 156.25 µg/m³

This sample is below the old residential SPM limit of 200 µg/m³, but you need a PM10 inlet before comparing it with the 100 µg/m³ PM10 limit. The EPA method uses standard volume, so correct flow to 25 °C and 1 atm if your report follows it.

Use this SPM analyzer calculator with your own filter weights and flows. It averages the start and end flow and prints the concentration.

SPM Concentration Calculator (µg/m³)
SPM concentration
156.25 µg/m³ from 1728.0 m³ of air

A 0.1 mg balance error on 1728 m³ shifts the result by only about 0.06 µg/m³, so flow usually decides your accuracy. Our note on measurement uncertainty in calibration shows how to combine balance, flow and time errors.

Quick Tip

Always use the average of start and end flow. Using only the start flow inflates the air volume and makes the dust look lower than it is.

How to Measure SPM with a High Volume Sampler

You measure SPM by conditioning and weighing a filter, running the sampler for 24 hours with logged flow, and reweighing the filter under the same conditions. The CPCB 2003 guideline asks for an average flow of at least 1.1 m³/min and a balance of 0.1 mg sensitivity or better.

Calibrate flowCheck against an orifice transfer standard.
Weigh the blankCondition 24 hours at 15 to 30 °C, below 50 percent RH.
Run 24 hoursLog start flow, end flow and elapsed time.
Fold and carryFold the filter dust side inward.
ReweighCondition again, weigh and calculate.

The flow device is often a manometer or a rotameter style indicator with its own calibration chart. Treat it like a mass flow controller, because every percent of flow error becomes a percent of SPM error.

A weighing lab that follows ISO 17025 requirements keeps check weight, temperature and humidity records. An auditor asks for that record when someone questions a reading.

SPM Analyzer Troubleshooting: Common Faults and Fixes

Most bad SPM analyzer readings come from low flow, moisture on the filter or a short run, not from the electronics. Work through the flowchart in order before you change any setting.

SymptomLikely causeFix
Flow drops earlyHeavy dust or worn brushesShorter run, new brushes
Negative weight gainDamp blank or lost fibresCondition 24 h, use forceps
High on humid morningsMoisture read as dustCheck inlet heater
Streaks at filter edgeGasket leakReplace gasket
BAM flat zeroTape not advancingReload tape, self test

Continuous analyzers often feed a DCS, so test the loop with a 4 to 20 mA signal conversion check and confirm the scaling. Store hourly values in the DCS historian to match them with plant events.

Moisture is the main enemy of optical and beta readings. The BAM 1020 has an actively controlled inlet heater, and a capacitive RH sensor at the inlet shows whether it is working.

Do You Know?

The Met One BAM 1020 was the first instrument with US EPA equivalent method status for continuous PM2.5, and one tape roll lasts over 70 days.

How to Select an SPM Analyzer for a Plant or City Station

Select an SPM analyzer by fixing the parameter the regulator wants first, then the data interval, and only then the method and brand. A manual sampler suits weekly compliance runs, while a beta or TEOM monitor suits continuous reporting.

  • Inlet matches the consent order: TSP, PM10 or PM2.5.
  • Method is listed in the 2009 NAAQS.
  • Range covers your worst day near coal yards.
  • Inlet heater for coastal and monsoon sites.
  • Outputs: 4 to 20 mA, Modbus and data logger.
  • Local service and spares in India.

If the SPM analyzer shares a shelter with gas analyzers, plan power and sample lines together, as our guide on sample conditioning systems explains.

SPM Analyzer FAQ

What is the difference between SPM, PM10 and PM2.5 in air quality?

SPM covers all airborne particles up to about 25 to 50 µm, while PM10 and PM2.5 are fractions at 10 µm and 2.5 µm.

So SPM is always the largest number. The 2009 NAAQS limits only PM10 and PM2.5, at 100 and 60 µg/m³ for 24 hours.

How to calculate SPM concentration from filter weight step by step?

Subtract the clean filter weight from the loaded weight, multiply by 10⁶ and divide by air volume in m³.

For example, 0.2700 g collected at 1.20 m³/min for 1440 minutes gives 1728 m³. The SPM is 270000 divided by 1728, or 156.25 µg/m³.

Which SPM analyzer method is best for continuous monitoring in India?

Beta attenuation is the usual choice because it gives hourly mass readings and is listed in the 2009 NAAQS.

TEOM is the other listed continuous method. Light scattering units are cheaper but need a correction factor from gravimetric samples before you trust the SPM analyzer value.

Why does my high volume sampler show negative weight gain on the filter?

Negative gain usually means the blank filter held moisture when first weighed or lost fibres in handling.

Condition both weighings for 24 hours below 50 percent humidity. Use clean forceps and check the balance zero with a known check weight before each weighing session.

What flow rate does a high volume SPM analyzer sampler use?

A high volume sampler runs at 1.1 to 1.7 m³/min, and CPCB asks for an average of at least 1.1 m³/min.

That gives about 1600 to 2400 m³ of air in 24 hours. PM2.5 samplers and the BAM 1020 use only 16.67 L/min.

What We Learn Today

  • SPM means suspended particulate matter, and PM10 and PM2.5 are its smaller size fractions that the 2009 NAAQS now limits in India.
  • An SPM analyzer works by filter weighing, beta attenuation, light scattering or TEOM, and weighing remains the reference that checks the others.
  • SPM in µg/m³ equals filter weight gain times one million divided by air volume, so accurate flow and run time decide the result.
